messages:
Avery K.: hey team, I'm taking the overnight primary (GMT-5). primary: Avery K., secondary: Jonah. I'm going to run a quick sweep of the Dedicated pool autoscale settings before I step away. :wave:

Jonah: thanks — noted. any specific gaps to call out?

Avery K.: yeah two things i saw in the last hour: 1) a couple of low-level KV cache misses on the european-dedicated pool (spike around 02:14 UTC) that bumped p95 token latency ~120ms, 2) one routing rule that falls back to a larger model variant without quota — could cause cost spikes if it keeps flipping.

Priya: do we have a quick runbook for the KV cache thrash? last time we nuked caches and warmed prefixes which helped.

Avery K.: OpsRunbookBot: runbook link below — short checklist at top. https://redwood.internal/runbooks/kv-cache-fallback

OpsRunbookBot: RUNBOOK: KV Cache thrash -> https://redwood.internal/runbooks/kv-cache-fallback. Steps: 1) identify impacted pods 2) toggle prefix cache retention to 30s 3) warm hot-prefixes 4) scale down and back up isolated worker groups if needed.

Maya: paging question — if we see another page for latency > 200ms on p95 should secondary be paged automatically or we manually @Jonah?

Avery K.: paging policy: severity 2 (p95 >200ms) pages both primary and secondary. incident-bot should handle that. If it doesn't, manual @Jonah and @Maya.

incident-bot: ALERT (sev2) — p95 token latency crossed 200ms on dedicated-eu-1. Triggered at 2026-03-14T02:32:11Z. Pager routed to oncall-primary and oncall-secondary. Link: https://redwood.internal/incidents/2487654321

Jonah: i'm on the page. grabbing logs and checking routing fallbacks now.

Priya: i'll take customer impact triage — which routes are affected? any paid customers on dedicated-eu-1 we should flag?

Avery K.: Priya, customer list: use this internal inventory (read-only): https://redwood.internal/tenants/dedicated-eu-1. Check top 5 by qps. If any SLA customers hit errors, escalate to support-oncall.

Jonah: quick findings: traffic shows increased KV-miss ratio on workers-7..10, and a small spike of fallback to model-raven-large-1 on route /v1/generate-chat. Batching looks normal.

Maya: any immediate mitigations we want to try?

Jonah: steps I'm doing now:
1) pin route to raven-medium-1 (compatible variant) to stop expensive fallback
2) flip prefix retention to 30s on workers-7..10
3) warm top 20 user prefixes via curl loop

Avery K.: add notes to the thread when you run each step. I'll coordinate customer triage and open an incident doc.

Jonah: 02:36Z — pinned /v1/generate-chat to raven-medium-1 via admin API:
```
POST https://api.redwood.internal/admin/routes/pin
{
  "route": "/v1/generate-chat",
  "model": "raven-medium-1",
  "reason": "mitigate costy fallback during KV thrash"
}
```
Response 200.

Jonah: 02:37Z — changed retention on workers-7..10:
```
kubectl exec -n inference worker-7 -- /bin/sh -c "curl -s -X POST localhost:8080/_admin/cache?retention=30"
kubectl exec -n inference worker-8 -- /bin/sh -c "curl -s -X POST localhost:8080/_admin/cache?retention=30"
```
Status: 200 for both.

Jonah: 02:41Z — warming prefixes (short script):
```
for p in $(cat top-prefixes.txt); do
  curl -s -X POST https://dedicated-eu-1.redwood/api/v1/generate -d "{\"prompt\": \"$p\"}" &
done
```
Backgrounded, warming in progress.

incident-bot: NOTE — paging suppressed after remediation steps posted by oncall. Monitor for 10m.

Priya: triage update: five customers had <2% error increase, no SLA breaches yet. Notifying support for two mid-market customers who run high-QPS.

Maya: any risk of the pin causing regressions (quality) on the pinned model?

Avery K.: quality risk: small. Raven-medium-1 is compatible for chat paths. If customers complain, we can rollback to multi-model routing with throttled fallback. Document step in incident doc.

Jonah: 02:52Z — worker-9 showed OOMs right before spike, I've cordoned it and restarted the pod.

Jonah: `kubectl cordon worker-9 && kubectl delete pod worker-9 -n inference`

Avery K.: good. add to incident doc: suspected root cause = transient KV backend lag + one noisy pod OOM causing cache pressure.

Priya: creating incident postmortem doc now: https://redwood.internal/incidents/2487654321/postmortem-draft

Maya: runbook pointers for quick reference (shortlinks):
- KV cache thrash: https://redwood.internal/r/kv-thrash (one-page cheatsheet)
- Model pin rollback: https://redwood.internal/r/model-pin-rollback
- Pod emergency restart: https://redwood.internal/r/pod-restart-cheat

Avery K.: handoff notes for next primary (Jonah if you take over at 06:00 UTC):
- watch dedicated-eu-1 p95 for 30m (threshold 180ms)
- monitor worker OOMs and cordon if necessary
- leave model pin in place until KV miss < 5% for 20m
- escalate to infra if KV backend error rate > 1%

Jonah: I can take the next primary block. leaving quick checklist in the oncall doc.

incident-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED — p95 returned to baseline. Resolution time: 20 minutes. Postmortem assigned to Priya.

Avery K.: thanks all. final note: add the exact `curl` warming script to the postmortem and the runbook. Also mark this incident with tag `kv-cache-thrash` and `routing-fallback`.

Priya: will do. adding remediation commands and timeline.

Maya: thanks — i'll update the console dashboard with a short annotation for the time window. :white_check_mark:

Jonah: handover accepted. handing primary to me at 06:00 UTC.

Avery K.: handing off. good work team. :thumbsup:
